items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: you still study Mozart, you know and Weber, and older composers.

ctx.x: Well I’m going to leapfrog a few decades. Is learning tunes for the current jazz student as important as it was back then? The reason I’m asking is partly technology that a student now can have hundreds of tunes on their phones or on their iPad, and it’s been my experience that they seem less inclined to memorize things.

I don’t know. The standard tunes, it’s sort of like if you’re playing classical clarinet let’s say, you still study Mozart, you know and Weber, and older composers. And the standard tunes are sort of a repertoire that I know our students at Eastman develop and work on. But you know they don’t stay stuck in playing standard tunes. They are also moving into their own thing, and using the information and the skills that they develop you know as playing by ear and learning these different standards. They apply that…
